content.title: About
content.content: Roma tomatoes are a variety of dense, meaty tomatoes with bright red skin, commonly used in cooking for sauces, pastes, and casseroles. They have a sweet‑tart flavor, few seeds, and low water content, making them ideal for thick sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Roma variety was developed in the United States in the early 20th century and quickly became popular for its shape and texture.
Roma tomatoes are often called "paste tomatoes" because they yield less juice than other varieties.
In Italy this variety is known as "Pomodoro Roma" and is a staple in traditional marinara and Bolognese sauces.
Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that gives them their vivid red color.
There are several Roma variants, including "Black Roma" with a dark‑red skin.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Roma tomatoes provide a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Lycopene and oxidative protection
items.content: Lycopene in red tomatoes has antioxidant properties and may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Heart‑healthy potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, and the low sodium content makes Roma tomatoes heart‑friendly.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Roma tomatoes are low‑calorie, making them a good choice for weight‑conscious diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes, such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of tomatoes can irritate the stomach in individuals with gastritis or ulcer disease.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic tomatoes, it is advisable to wash them thoroughly to reduce any pesticide residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Roma tomatoes are frequently used in sauces, soups, stews, and casseroles. They can be roasted, sautéed, braised, or eaten fresh in salads. For a richer flavor, tomatoes can be briefly fried in olive oil before adding to dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Roma tomatoes at room temperature, away from direct sunlight, if you plan to use them within a few days. For longer storage, place them in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, though this may alter their texture.
